subject: Request: Processor assurance package and DPIA annex for HealthFirst onboarding
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthfirst.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@healthfirst.com
Date: 2027-06-19T09:12:00+02:00
Subject: Processor assurance package and DPIA annex needed for onboarding

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our security & privacy intake we need a small set of documents to finish legal review and the DPIA for our deployment: 1) a current Art. 28 subprocessor inventory with subprocessors, country of processing, and purpose; 2) an Art. 30-type processing activities ledger export summarising categories of personal data, retention periods, and legal basis; and 3) a draft DPIA annex / template we can attach to our contract (we can add project-specific fields afterwards).

Would you be able to provide those items and a short note on whether any EU→US transfers rely on standard contractual clauses or other safeguards? Also, we routinely ask for a brief control attestation for log retention, access controls, and encryption in transit/at rest. If you have an internal contact at Redwood who owns the subprocessor list & ledger export, please loop them in.

We have a soft deadline of end-of-week for our onboarding sprint. Please let us know if that is feasible or if we should schedule a short sync to align scope.

Regards,
Laura Chen
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthFirst

Attachments: none
From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthfirst.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-19T10:01:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Processor assurance package and DPIA annex needed for onboarding

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for; I’m attaching the current exports and a DPIA annex template for HealthFirst to review. Quick notes up front:

- Subprocessors: the attached sheet lists processors, locations, data categories and purpose. We mark any non-EU hosts and whether SCCs apply.
- Art. 30 ledger: exported CSV has processing categories, retention summary, and a column with the processing legal basis used by the product.
- DPIA annex: draft PDF with sections you can edit (processing description, risk mitigations, data flow diagram reference).

Regarding transfers: for customers in the EU we use European Commission approved SCCs between Redwood and any US-based subprocessors by default; when customers require additional safeguards we support on-prem or EU-only deployment options. I note in the subprocessor sheet which entries imply cross-border processing.

For the control attestation: we can include a short statement on (1) encryption in transit (TLS1.2+), (2) encryption at rest for persistent stores, and (3) retention and access logging. I’ll also ask our cloud assurance partner (Marco Silva) to provide a short operational note on log retention/forwarding.

If the attachments work, we can follow up with any redlines. If you prefer a call, I’m free 15:30–16:30 CET today.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments (sent): redwood_art28_article30_ledger_export.csv; dpia-annex-v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20270614.xlsx
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-19T11:24:00+02:00
Subject: Fwd: Processor assurance package and DPIA annex needed for onboarding

Looping in our legal intake notes — quick internal plan:

- Confirm the CSV includes retention fields and a contact column for each subprocessor (action: Jonas to update export if missing).
- Prepare an Art. 28 cover statement for signature (standard DPA language) and a short attestation template for operations (1 paragraph).
- Marco (cloud assurance) should provide the log retention paragraph and confirm whether logs are stored in EU-only buckets for HealthFirst (action: Soojin to confirm).

Jonas — can you check the ledger export for the retention/processing-basis columns? If not present, add them and return by 13:00 so we can send to Laura by EOD. I’ll draft the attestation language and put it in Drive.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Customer Contracts

I checked the export — retention column exists but some old rows are missing the legal_basis field (legacy models). I patched those with the current default basis (performance of a contract / legitimate interests where applicable) and attached the updated CSV path in Drive. Also flagged three subprocessors that use US-based analytics; I added a note recommending SCC confirmation.

We should be able to send to HealthFirst by 15:30 if Soojin confirms the attestation paragraph and Marco’s log note are in. I’ll also prepare a one-paragraph summary of our SCC fallback for the email.

-Jonas
Senior Privacy Engineer

Subject: Re: Processor assurance package and DPIA annex needed for onboarding — package delivered

Hi Laura / Marco —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are the files we discussed and a short operational attestation below. Files + Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/HealthFirst/Onboarding/Privacy-Pack (same files attached for convenience).

Operational attestation (summary):
Redwood Inference confirms that for the services provided to HealthFirst: (1) data in transit is protected using TLS 1.2+; (2) persistent customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256; (3) access to production systems is limited to authorised personnel and logged; (4) retention for identified personal data follows the retention periods in the attached ledger; (5) standard contractual clauses are used to govern transfers to US-based subprocessors by default. Detailed evidence and CSV export are in the attached files.

Next steps:
- Please review the DPIA annex (dpia-annex-v1.pdf) and redline where you need project-specific fields.
- If HealthFirst would like an EU-only hosting option, we can produce a scoped quote and timeline.

If you want a short call to review the package, I’m available 16:00–16:30 CET today.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_art28_article30_ledger_export.csv; dpia-annex-v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20270614.xlsx
